title: Open direct-image finiteness for all-continuous algebraic-closure coefficients
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the topology of the extended $\ell$-adic absolute value. Let $\Lambda$ be the commutative condensed ring with $\Lambda(S)=C(S,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ for every profinite set $S$, with pointwise ring operations [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Let $U,X$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ a quasi-compact open $k$-immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Pull the coefficient ring back from the point, $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ for $T=U,X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. If $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_U})$ is bounded and each cohomology module has finite constant local models on a finite constructible stratification, then $Rj_*K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X})$ is bounded and each of its cohomology modules has finite constant local models on a finite constructible stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Here $Rj_*$ is the ordinary total right derived module-object direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. All continuous coefficient functions are admitted, with no assumption that their images lie in a single finite subextension. The statement asserts neither finite Tor amplitude nor any proper-image or compactification conclusion.

proof.text: Write $B=\Lambda$ and $A_E(P)=C(P,E)$ for each finite intermediate field $E\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. The standing schemes, and their locally closed subschemes, are Noetherian and qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], applied over the spectrum of the field. Write $\mathcal B(T)$ for bounded finite-constant-model constructible $B_T$-complexes. By [lem-sfb-continuous-qbar-constructible-generators], $\mathcal B(X)$ is triangulated and $\mathcal B(U)$ is generated under finitely many shifts, isomorphisms and triangles by $(a_!L)[0]$ with $a:S\hookrightarrow U$ locally closed and $L$ lisse over $B_S$. All objects used here are bounded below. On that subcategory the ordinary total derived functor is its bounded-below version [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], which is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] applied to the additive left exact module direct image. Its inverse image of $\mathcal B(X)$ is consequently a replete triangulated class. It suffices to put every such generator in that class.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open image: reduction to the finite lisse generators, using the all-continuous generator theorem.

proof.text: For a generator $(a_!L)[0]$ on $U$, apply [lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-finite-stage-devissage] with $T=U$. It supplies a finite triangle filtration with pieces $G_t\cong B_U\otimes^L_{A_{E_t,U}}C_t$, where $E_t/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $C_t\in\mathcal B_{E_t}(U)$. The comparison is $B_U$-linear in the ordinary ambient derived category. Triangulatedness from step 1 reduces the assertion to these finitely many pieces.

source.place: Paragraph (3), source finite-field dévissage; returned steps 2--3 are the separate finite-stage-devissage obligation.

proof.text: Fix a piece and abbreviate $E_t,C_t$ by $E,C$. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-open-direct-image-constructible] with coefficient $E$: $C$ is bounded constructible and $j$ is quasi-compact open between separated finite-type schemes over $k$, with $\operatorname{char}k\ne\ell$. Thus $M=Rj_{*,A_E}C\in\mathcal B_E(X)$. By [lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-scalar-constructibility], $B_X\otimes^L_{A_{E,X}}M\in\mathcal B(X)$. The canonical comparison [lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-open-scalar-comparison] identifies this object with $Rj_{*,B}(B_U\otimes^L_{A_{E,U}}C)\cong Rj_{*,B}G_t$. Consequently every piece has image in $\mathcal B(X)$, and the finite filtrations of step 2 and generation of step 1 give the claim for $K$. Only finitely many intervals occur, so their minima and maxima give boundedness. Identity and empty opens give the identity and zero functors.
